chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about nabidh whose boiling had settled, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden.'

He said: And I asked him about the containers, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the pumpkin (container), the asphalted one, and you have added the hantam, meaning the clay, and the asphalted means the bitumen that is in the skin bag and is poured into the mixture to make it better for the wine.
He said: And I asked him about the green urns and the lead, so he said: There is no problem with them.

key_terms.الدُّبَّاء: Al-dubba': A container made from a dried pumpkin or gourd.
key_terms.المُزَفَّت: Al-muzaffat: A container coated or lined with bitumen/asphalt.
key_terms.الْجِرَار: Al-jirar: Large earthenware urns or jars.
key_terms.الْحَنْتَم: Al-hantam: A type of clay or earthenware container.
key_terms.الْخَوَاب: Al-khawa': A skin bag or vessel.
key_terms.مُسْكِر: Muskir: Intoxicant; that which causes intoxication.
key_terms.نَبِيذ: Nabidh: A drink made by fermenting dates or raisins in water.

ai.seo_question: What containers are prohibited for fermenting nabidh in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific material restrictions for nabidh containers, linking the prohibition of certain vessels to the prevention of intoxication (khamr). It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the general principle of 'kullu muskirin haram' and the specific juristic application regarding materials like pumpkin and bitumen, which were known to impart or preserve intoxicating qualities. The permission of green urns and lead underscores the practical emphasis on material purity and inertness in preserving the drink's state.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban Al Kalby, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), said, ‘I asked himasws about Nabeez, the boiling of which had settled.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the containers.

So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww had forbidden from the pumpkin (as a container for fermentation), and the asphalted pot, and you have increased Al-Hantam, meaning the clay, and the asphalt meaning the bitumen which happens to be in the skin bag, and it is poured in the mixture for it to better the wine’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the green urns and the lead, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with these’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbiy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about al- Nabidh which has stopped boiling.

He (the Imam) said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ’All intoxicating substances are unlawful/ I then asked him (the Imam) about utensils. He (the Imam) has stated this Hadith. ’The Messenger of Allah, O Allah grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to your cause, has prohibited the use of al-Diba ’ (pumpkins) used in fermenting al-Nabidh.

Also prohibited for such use is al-Hantam (the pot made of asphalt-coated clay), to which you have added oiled pottery, and al-Ghadar (what is made of palm tree trunks coated with asphalt) in which wine is brewed to make it of better quality.’
I asked him (the Imam) about large green containers and lead. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
